notes.text: In this section, I want to elaborate in subsections with diagrams and code snippets the difference between use client directives usage in the application's components and a monorepo isolated ui library for components.  in the case of a dedicated ui library in the monorepo, it affects how we build those components.  Components that have interactive parts should try to expose both the structure/containers and outer parts that are non interactive along with the interactive smaller parts.  So a sidebar component should not be an all or nothing sidebar where we provide items={[...]} as an array of JS objects with properties like icon and onclick, it should be a container ocmponent Sidebar and also expose things like SidebarItem or SidebarLinkItem, or SidebarButtonItem so that the interactivity can be isolated to just the smaller parts that need "use client".  This allows the overall usage in the consuming application to have the flexibility to not be forced into treating the entire sidebar it renders (using the ui library sidebar) into a client component because the sidebar itself can be rendered without interactivity, and the interactive leaves which represent the individual items in the sidebar can be isolated in separate files with on click handlers (if it needs on click) with "use client" but if it's a link item and can use an href then the onclick handler is not needed at all and it doesn't need the directive.  This is the general idea there.  I also want to show code snippets/examples of how to "internalize" third party components, so that we use a single file that wraps the third-party component and adds "use client" so that the third-party component itself is just the leaf, rather than every composite component that imports and uses the third party component directly being forced into "use client" usage.

The problem is that they show empty states as if they are the same size as the content was when the figma had data in it - but not an empty state or consideration for cases where its flipping between that empty state and a data view where there is just 1 row, for instance, or 300 rows.  In other words, it's often the case that the comp will include a view with 8 data points, showing the 8 data points in a container that has a random height constraint and isn't thinking about what happens when that height constraint is not known or is pushing other content around.  We don't know how big the view should be to show the empty state if we don't know how many rows or data points there are - and we will never know how many rows or data points there are so we have t ofigure out how to swap both states in a way where it doesn't push everything else around.

notes.text: I want to expand here and talk more about how traditional prisma usage is built to use prisma directly inside of server actions, eliminating the need for an API.  This applies to other ORMS as well.  But it should say that while that is optimal for latency, flexibility, speed and avoiding an API that is overly copuled to a UI, it is still okay to use a dedicated backend layer or cetnralized API - but it should be direct and not through a proxy in API routes.  I want to include code snippets showing usage with Prisma directly in server actions, but also the HTTP snippets where we go to a centralized API.  It should show prisma examples in the context of error handling surface - and type safety - where we can simply fetch just the data we need in that one action and tialor the way we write the action so that it handles the error cases automatically for that specific action in context - and not 100 other actions that use the same API endpoint (which is where the API coupling gets in).  IT should be like "if the findUnique is null, then we indicate in the return type that it does not exist with some type of { error } or 'message' or something - but when we go through an HTTP API, a 404 could also mean that the actual endpoint doesn't exist... right?  It could mean that the model doesn't exist too - just as an example for teh error surface and decision making from returns/responses.  But it should say and focus on the fact that even going through a central APi is infinitely better than going through a proxy when we can avoid it - the proxy is not needed for server actions and it widens the error surface and hurts type safety.

target.snippet: 5.10 Server actions and the HTTP middleman

notes.resolution: Section 5.10 expanded with two subsections and snippets: "The direct version: the ORM inside the action" (Prisma findUnique with a per-action select, null as an unambiguous domain answer returned as typed { error }, revalidateTag on success) and "The centralized API, called directly: still fine" (fetch to a dedicated backend from the action, with the 404-ambiguity comment: gone? route moved? renamed?; types end at the HTTP boundary; the endpoint's error conventions serve every caller so they fit none). Closes with the gradient: ORM in action optimal (latency, flexibility, end-to-end types, no UI-coupled API), centralized API called directly a legitimate organizational step down, the proxy through your own API routes the only indefensible rung.
